name: Time-Entry Draft from Calendar

parameters.content:
## Time-Entry Draft from Calendar

### How it works

1. The workflow triggers every morning to fetch and filter billable calendar events from the previous day.
2. It fetches related Clio matters and generates narrative prompts for time entries using an AI service.
3. The generated narratives are validated and a digest including approval links is compiled and emailed.
4. Webhook triggers handle approval link visits and confirmation of time entries with further validation.
5. Approved time entries are posted to Clio, logged, and confirmation pages are served.
6. Errors during confirmation are captured and responded to appropriately.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Configure Google Calendar API credentials for event fetching.
- [ ] Set up Clio API credentials and base URL variables.
- [ ] Set up AI service credentials for narrative generation.
- [ ] Configure email sending credentials for daily digest emails.
- [ ] Configure webhook URLs and ensure public access for approval and confirmation links.

## Daily trigger and date builder

Starts the workflow on a daily schedule and builds yesterday's UTC date range to fetch calendar events.

## Fetch and filter calendar events

Fetches yesterday's calendar events and filters for billable events containing matter references.

## Clio matters retrieval and filtering

Fetches Clio matters by reference and filters for exact matches to link calendar events.

## Generate narrative or note

Builds AI narrative prompts for matched matters or notes for unmatched matters.

## Build and merge digest entries

Constructs approval links in digest entries, merges branches, and builds combined digest.

## Compliance logging and email sending

Executes compliance logging sub-workflow and sends daily time entry email with digest.

## Approval link webhook handling

Handles webhook trigger from approval link clicks and builds the attorney's approval confirmation page.

## Time entry confirmation webhook

Receives webhook for time entry confirmations and validates incoming requests.

## Invalid confirmation response

Builds and sends a response for invalid or failed confirmation validations.

## Post approved time entries

Posts approved time entries to Clio and triggers approval logging workflow.

## Approval success response pages

Builds and sends confirmation pages after successful time entry approvals.

nodes.name: Trigger Every Morning at 7am
nodes.notes:
Fires every morning at 7am (n8n server timezone) and covers all of the previous calendar day — running daily (including weekends) rather than weekday-only means a Monday run still picks up anything from Sunday, and nothing is ever skipped because of which day it happened to fall on.

This is the only thing that starts a digest run.

nodes.name: Build Yesterday UTC Date Range
nodes.notes: entry_date is used later as the date on the Clio time entry itself — it's yesterday's calendar date, not today's (the day the digest actually arrives).

nodes.name: Fetch Calendar Events From Yesterday
nodes.notes:
Reads yesterday's events from the connected Google Calendar — same Calendar API and 'Predefined Credential Type' / googleCalendarOAuth2Api pattern the Court Deadline Calculator (NTC-16) already uses for writing events, just GET instead of POST.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search 'Google Calendar OAuth2 API' → connect the attorney's Google account → save as 'Google Calendar account' (reuse NTC-16's if already deployed).

FIRM_ATTORNEY_CALENDAR_ID defaults to 'primary' (the connected account's own calendar) — set it to a specific calendar ID/email if the firm uses a shared or delegated calendar instead.

nodes.name: Extract Billable Events With Matter Ref
nodes.notes: Any '[...]' bracket found anywhere in the title is treated as the matter reference — put it at the start (e.g. '[2026-CH-042] Client call') for readability, but position doesn't matter to the parser. An event with no bracket, or an all-day event, is silently excluded -- not flagged as an error, since most calendar events are never meant to be billable.

nodes.name: If Events Are Billable
nodes.notes:
Yes (at least one tagged event yesterday) → process each one.
No (nothing tagged — a day with no billable calendar activity, or the attorney forgot to tag anything) → route to Skip.

nodes.name: Skip Non-Billable Events
nodes.notes: No calendar events were tagged with a matter reference yesterday. No digest sent — an empty digest every day would train the attorney to ignore it.

nodes.name: Split Billable Events Into Items
nodes.notes: Fans out into one item per tagged event — everything downstream through the digest email processes one event's draft time entry at a time.

nodes.name: Fetch Clio Matters By Reference
nodes.notes:
Clio's query parameter is a broad text search, not an exact match — same pattern as PAC-58's contact lookup — the next step filters down to an exact display_number match before trusting anything.

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as PAC-18/20/55/57/58/59/61 — reuse it if already deployed.

nodes.name: Filter Exact Clio Matter Match
nodes.notes: Reads event metadata from 'Split Into One Item Per Event' explicitly, not $json, since the matters.json call above replaced the item's data with its own response.

nodes.name: If Clio Matter Found
nodes.notes:
Yes (the bracket tag matched exactly one real Clio matter) → draft a narrative.
No (no exact match — likely a typo in the tag) → flag it in the digest for manual entry instead of guessing which matter was meant.

nodes.name: Build Note For Unmatched Matter
nodes.notes: No Clio API call, no narrative, no approve link — just a note in the digest so the attorney knows this event needs manual attention instead of it silently vanishing.

nodes.name: Build Narrative Prompt For Entry
nodes.notes: Deliberately metadata-only — the prompt never has access to a linked document or email body, only what's already visible on the calendar event itself (title, description, attendees, duration). Model: claude-sonnet-4-6; switch to claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 to reduce cost.

nodes.name: Post Narrative Generation Request
nodes.notes:
Sends the prompt to Claude (Anthropic) and receives the narrative as JSON.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search 'Header Auth' → Name: 'Anthropic API key' → Header Name: 'x-api-key' → Header Value: your key from console.anthropic.com. Reuse the same credential as PAC-31/50/60 if already deployed.

nodes.name: Parse And Validate Narrative Response
nodes.notes: Two-layer safety check, same pattern as PAC-31/50/60: Claude's own self-report is Layer 1, an independent keyword regex scan is Layer 2. Also enforces a 200-character cap so narratives stay concise and don't get silently truncated by Clio's own field limits later.

nodes.name: If Narrative Is Approved
nodes.notes:
Yes (both safety layers passed) → build the approve link.
No (flagged by either layer) → the item already has everything 'Aggregate Digest Entries' needs (event_title, duration_hours, reason) — it skips straight to the merge with no approve link, since there's nothing safe to approve yet.

nodes.name: Build Approval Link And Digest
nodes.notes: N8N_PUBLIC_URL should be your n8n instance's public base URL (e.g. 'https://your-n8n.example.com', no trailing slash) — needed because this link goes into an email and has to be a full absolute URL, not a relative path. If unset, the link will be missing its domain and won't work; set this Variable before activating.

nodes.name: Merge All Digest Entry Branches
nodes.notes: Waits for every event's outcome — unmatched, flagged, or ready to approve — before the digest is assembled. Without this, the digest could be built and sent before every event's branch has finished, silently dropping whichever ran slowest (same risk PAC-57's notes describe for its DocuSign/Google Docs branches).

nodes.name: Aggregate All Digest Entries
nodes.notes: Splits every event's outcome into a 'Ready To Approve' section (with working Approve buttons) and a 'Needs Attention' section (unmatched matter tags or flagged narratives, no button since there's nothing to approve yet). Builds both a styled HTML version and a plain-text fallback.

nodes.name: Execute Compliance Logging Workflow
nodes.notes: Logs the digest compilation to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet. This is internal record-keeping, not a client message — opt-out checking doesn't apply here. The actual time-entry creation gets its own separate audit log entry when approved.

value.message: ={{ $json.ready_count + ' ready, ' + $json.flagged_count + ' flagged out of yesterday\'s tagged calendar events.' }}

nodes.name: Send Daily Time Entry Email
nodes.notes:
Delivers the digest to the attorney with both a styled HTML version and a plain-text fallback. Reads explicitly from 'Aggregate Digest Entries' by name rather than $json — the guardrail call immediately upstream replaced the item's json.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

nodes.name: Approve Link Webhook Trigger
nodes.notes:
Entry point when the attorney clicks 'Review & Approve' in the digest email. Deliberately does NOT create the time entry on this GET request — it only shows a review page. This is what protects against email security scanners (Microsoft Defender Safe Links, Proofmark, Proofpoint, etc.) that automatically pre-fetch every link in an inbound email — if this step created the entry directly, those scanners would silently 'approve' every draft before the attorney ever saw it.

Activate the workflow, then copy this node's Production URL's domain into the N8N_PUBLIC_URL Variable.

nodes.name: Build Approval Confirmation Page
nodes.notes: 'action="confirm-time-entry"' is a relative URL, resolved by the browser against this page's own address — no need to hardcode the n8n domain a second time here.

nodes.name: Respond With Approval Confirmation
nodes.notes: Returns the review page. Same pattern as PAC-55's dismiss-confirmation page.

nodes.name: Confirm Time Entry Webhook
nodes.notes: Only a real button click reaches this webhook — the review page's form submits here via POST, which pre-fetch scanners don't do. This is the only place in the whole workflow that actually writes a time entry to Clio.

nodes.name: Validate Time Entry Confirmation
nodes.notes: Guards against a malformed or tampered form submission reaching the Clio API call. A genuine submission from 'Build Confirmation Page' will always have every required field, since they're all hidden inputs carried through unchanged.

nodes.name: If Confirmation Request Valid
nodes.notes:
Yes → create the real Clio time entry.
No (missing fields — a broken or tampered request) → show an error page instead. Nothing is written to Clio either way until this passes.

nodes.name: Build Invalid Confirmation Error
nodes.notes: No Clio entry is ever created for an invalid request — this page just explains why.

nodes.name: Respond With Confirmation Error
nodes.notes: Returns the error page built by 'Build Invalid Request Error Page'. Same pattern as PAC-55's dismiss-confirmation page.

nodes.name: Post New Clio Time Entry
nodes.notes:
Creates the real billable time entry in Clio. The Activities API's exact shape here (type: 'TimeEntry', quantity in seconds, the user/matter sub-object format) follows Clio's general v4 REST conventions but hasn't been independently confirmed against a live account during authoring — check developer.clio.com and your first real confirmation before relying on this, and verify the created entry's duration matches what was shown on the review page (quantity is assumed to be seconds, not hours).

FIRM_ATTORNEY_CLIO_USER_ID: find this in Clio under Settings → Users.

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as the rest of this workflow.

'Never Error' is on so a failed create still shows the attorney a clear result (via the next step reading this response) rather than a raw HTTP error page.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ data: { type: 'TimeEntry', matter: { id: Number($json.matter_id) }, date: $json.entry_date, quantity: Math.round(Number($json.duration_hours) * 3600), note: $json.narrative, user: { id: Number($vars.FIRM_ATTORNEY_CLIO_USER_ID) } } }) }}

nodes.name: Execute Approval Logging Workflow
nodes.notes: Logs the approval to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet. Reads explicitly from 'Validate Confirm Request' rather than $json, since the Clio API call immediately upstream replaced the item's json with its own response.

value.matter_id: ={{ $('Validate Time Entry Confirmation').item.json.matter_display_number || String($('Validate Time Entry Confirmation').item.json.matter_id) }}

nodes.name: Build Success Confirmation Page
nodes.notes: Reads explicitly from 'Validate Confirm Request' by name — both the Clio create call and the compliance-log call in between replaced the item's json with their own responses.

nodes.name: Respond With Approval Success Page
nodes.notes: Returns the success page built by 'Build Success Confirmation Page' -- this is the very last step, after the Clio time entry has actually been created and logged to compliance.

body.narrative: Telephone conference with opposing counsel regarding settlement terms.

query.narrative: Telephone conference with opposing counsel regarding settlement terms.

content.text: {"narrative": "Telephone conference with opposing counsel regarding custody schedule modification terms.", "is_narrative_safe": true}

main.node: Extract Billable Events With Matter Ref

description: Reads yesterday's calendar events tagged with a '[matter-ref]' in the title, matches each to a Clio matter, and drafts a factual billing narrative from the event's metadata only (title, description, attendees, duration -- never a linked document or email body) using the same two-layer safety check as the Content Repurposer (PAC-31). One daily digest email lists every draft with an Approve button; approving is a two-step confirmation (review page, then a real button click) rather than a single GET link, so email security scanners that pre-fetch links can't accidentally create a real billable time entry nobody reviewed. Replaces manual time entry and native partial-capture tools. Logs every digest and every approval to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet.
